top5.title: Nvidia risks losing the engineers behind its AI dominance
top5.description: After Jensen Huang’s resignation, Nvidia faces the risk of losing some of the engineers responsible for its chips and technical systems. Analysts believe this exodus could jeopardize the company’s AI roadmap.
top5.why: Nvidia’s potential loss of key AI-chip engineers could disrupt its product roadmap and threaten the company’s leadership in the rapidly expanding AI infrastructure market.

top5.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon, a powerful and cheaper coding model
top5.description: Google has announced Gemini 4 Neon, a model positioned between Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen. It ranks third on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and first in its Coding Agent ranking. Its API costs $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with a one-million-token context window.
top5.why: Google’s cheaper, high-performing Gemini 4 Neon coding model could intensify competition in AI-assisted software development and pressure rivals’ pricing.

top5.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Sales with more than 30 integrations
top5.description: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT for Sales, a plugin offering more than 30 integrations and capable of using customer data from Salesforce and HubSpot, among others.
top5.why: OpenAI’s ChatGPT for Sales brings AI directly into Salesforce, HubSpot and other enterprise workflows, signaling a major push to monetize customer and sales operations.

top5.title: Technology outages revive emergency preparedness
top5.description: A series of technology outages disrupted email, travel, investments, money transfers, and purchases. With no indication of a coordinated cyberattack, the incidents are nevertheless prompting many consumers to stock up on water, propane, and other emergency supplies.
top5.why: Repeated technology outages are exposing the fragility of critical digital infrastructure and prompting businesses and consumers to reconsider continuity and emergency-preparedness practices.

top5.title: Atlassian finds that AI speeds delivery without yet improving customer value
top5.description: According to Atlassian’s State of Product 2027 study, 80% of product professionals believe AI helps them deliver faster, but customers do not yet perceive that value sooner. The report also examines persistent limitations, including decision-making and reliance on instinct over customer data.
top5.why: Atlassian’s research highlights a widening gap between faster AI-driven delivery and measurable customer value, a warning that productivity gains are not yet translating into business outcomes.
